title: 1992 AHSME Problem 26
statement: Semicircle \(\widehat{AB}\) has center \(C\) and radius \(1.\) Point \(D\) is on \(\widehat{AB}\) and \(CD\perp AB.\) Extend \(\overline{BD}\) and \(\overline{AD}\) to \(E\) and \(F,\) respectively, so that circular arcs \(\widehat{AE}\) and \(\widehat{BF}\) have \(B\) and \(A\) as their respective centers. Circular arc \(\widehat{EF}\) has center \(D.\) The area of the shaded “smile,” \(AEFBDA,\) is

solutions.text:
Triangles \(ACD\) and \(BCD\) are isosceles right triangles, so \(AD=BD=\sqrt2,\) \(\angle ADB=90^\circ,\) and \(DE=DF=2-\sqrt2.\) The smile is the \(90^\circ\) sector \(EDF,\) plus the congruent \(45^\circ\) sectors \(ABE\) and \(BAF,\) minus triangle \(ABD\) and the original semicircle. Its area is \[ \begin{aligned} &\frac14\pi(2-\sqrt2)^2 +2\left(\frac18\pi\cdot2^2\right)\\ &\qquad-\frac12(2)(1)-\frac12\pi\\ &=2\pi-\pi\sqrt2-1. \end{aligned} \]

Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: Use \(AC=BC=CD=1\) to identify two isosceles right triangles and determine the relevant radii
Express the smile as one \(90^\circ\) sector plus two \(45^\circ\) sectors, then subtract triangle \(ABD\) and semicircle \(ADB\)
